_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED into src/data/index.ts. AF/G.22 population-priority push, 2026-08-13. Transcribed from a prior agent's verified findings (no new web research performed this round). Adds Niger's mining and petroleum revenue-sharing formulas (Code Minier Art. 95 and Code Pétrolier Art. 146, both 85%/15% state/commune splits) and the implementing Décret n°2007-184 (90/5/5 intra-commune spending split), all sourced via Niger's official 2022 EITI report quoting the underlying legal texts; a named commune-level budget document was searched for but not found.

reports.title: Code Minier — Loi n°2022-033 du 5 juillet 2022 (Article 95 : répartition des recettes minières)
reports.publisher: Présidence de la République / Assemblée Nationale (République du Niger)
reports.description: Article 95 of Niger's 2022 Code Minier (Loi n°2022-033 du 5 juillet 2022) fixes an 85%/15% split of mining revenue between the national budget and the budgets of communes in the producing region. Quoted verbatim as reproduced by Niger's official 2022 EITI report (Rapport ITIE Niger 2022, prepared by independent administrator BDO LLP under Niger's government-mandated EITI mechanism, citing DGTCP data), Section 5.2.17 'Transferts infranationaux', p.92: "L'article 95 du Code Minier précise que les recettes minières constituées par la redevance minière, la redevance superficiaire, les droits fixes, le produit de la taxe d'exploitation artisanale et le produit de la vente des cartes d'artisans miniers, sont réparties comme suit : - 85% pour le budget national ; et - 15% pour le budget des communes de la région concernée pour le financement du développement local." The same Article 95 text was independently corroborated via a mirror copy of the law hosted at droit-afrique.com's own reproduction (s3.amazonaws.com/rgi-documents, the URL used here as the node's document link). The droit-afrique.com original (www.droit-afrique.com/uploads/Niger-Loi-2022-33-miniere.pdf) returned a 403 error on every attempt, and a Google Drive copy linked from itieniger.ne could not be rendered as text, so no official Niger-government-hosted (Journal Officiel) copy of the law itself was reached this round; treat sourcing as one level removed (official EITI report quoting the law, corroborated by a private-sector legal-database mirror) rather than the raw Journal Officiel text.

reports.title: Code Pétrolier de la République du Niger (Article 146 nouveau : répartition des revenus pétroliers)
reports.publisher: Présidence de la République / Ministère du Pétrole (République du Niger)
reports.description: Article 146 (nouveau) of Niger's Code Pétrolier fixes an 85%/15% split of specified petroleum revenues (redevance ad valorem, droits fixes, redevance superficiaire, net of agent ristournes) between the national budget and the territorial collectivités (régions and communes) of extraction/exploitation zones. Downloaded directly from the website of the Ambassade du Niger en France (a Niger government diplomatic domain), quote: "85 % pour le budget national ; 15 % pour le budget des collectivités territoriales." Fuller context, corroborated verbatim (matching wording) in Niger's official 2022 EITI report (Rapport ITIE Niger 2022, p.57, §5.1.15): "les revenus constitués de la redevance ad valorem, les droits fixes et la redevance superficiaire, déduction faite des ristournes concédées aux agents du Ministère du Pétrole sont réparties comme suit : - 85% au budget de l'Etat ; et - 15% attribués aux régions et communes des zones d'extraction et d'exploitation pour le financement du développement local." Of the two revenue-sharing formulas found this round, this is the closer to a true government-hosted primary source, since ambassadeniger-fr.org is a Niger state domain rather than a third-party mirror.

reports.title: Décret n°2007-184/PRN/MI/D du 25 mai 2007 (Article 6 : affectation des transferts infranationaux miniers)
reports.publisher: Présidence de la République / Ministère de l'Intérieur (République du Niger)
reports.description: Décret n°2007-184/PRN/MI/D du 25 mai 2007, Article 6, sets a 90%/5%/5% intra-commune allocation formula for the mining-revenue transfers communes receive under Code Minier Article 95: 90% to investment, 5% to operating costs (fonctionnement), and 5% to technical support/monitoring-evaluation of local development activities by technical services. Quoted as cited within Niger's official 2022 EITI report (Rapport ITIE Niger 2022), Section 5.2.17 'Transferts infranationaux', p.92, the same section documenting the Code Minier Article 95 85/15 split: "Les municipalités bénéficiaires doivent utiliser les fonds reçus selon un mécanisme prévu par le Décret n°2007-184/PRN/MI/D du 25 mai 2007 qui dispose dans son article 6 que 90% des fonds sont destinés aux investissements, 5% au fonctionnement et 5% à l'appui technique aux municipalités ou au suivi et à l'évaluation des activités de développement par les services techniques." The mechanism is described as presently governing fund use, though the same report notes 2022 transfers under this scheme were still unpaid in arrears as of the report date ('la DGTCP n'a pas encore payé les transferts infranationaux de 2022'). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the décret's own primary text could not be located despite extensive searching this round — not found in justice.gouv.ne's 992-page 'Recueil thématique de textes législatifs et réglementaires' (full-text checked, zero matches for '2007-184'), not on FAOLEX, not on droit-afrique.com's index, and not on decentralisation-niger.net's 'Textes Fondamentaux'. This node rests entirely on the EITI report's citation/quotation of the décret, not on independently verified primary text; the url field below points to the EITI report (the only accessible source), not to the décret itself.

dependencies.basis: Both provisions are documented together, in the same source-document section (Rapport ITIE Niger 2022, §5.2.17, p.92), where the décret's 90/5/5 intra-commune spending formula is presented as governing how communes must use 'les fonds reçus' — i.e., the very mining-revenue transfers that Code Minier Article 95 assigns to them via the 85/15 national/commune split. Quote establishing the link: "Les municipalités bénéficiaires doivent utiliser les fonds reçus selon un mécanisme prévu par le Décret n°2007-184/PRN/MI/D du 25 mai 2007 qui dispose dans son article 6 que 90% des fonds sont destinés aux investissements, 5% au fonctionnement et 5% à l'appui technique aux municipalités..." The décret's applicability is contingent on Code Minier Art. 95 having generated the 15%-to-communes fund pool in the first place, so the décret's spending mechanism depends on the mining code's revenue-sharing formula rather than existing independently of it.

_dropped.why: Considered a cites/methodology_depends_on edge from the mining, petroleum, or décret nodes to the existing CGCT node (ne-ordonnance-2010-54-cgct), since the CGCT is Niger's general local-government code and might plausibly be the framework these sectoral revenue-sharing rules implement. Findings file explicitly checked the CGCT itself (Ordonnance 2010-54) for a numeric transfer-percentage article and found none — Article 7 only defers competency/financial-transfer mechanics to 'un plan graduel, fixé par décret pris en Conseil des Ministres' — confirming the CGCT node correctly has no formula of its own, but this also means the CGCT's own text does not name or cite Code Minier Art. 95, Code Pétrolier Art. 146, or Décret 2007-184 as the décret(s) it defers to. Additionally, Décret 2007-184 (2007) predates Ordonnance 2010-54 (2010), so a citation running from the décret to the CGCT is chronologically implausible. No textual citation link exists in the findings file connecting these instruments to the CGCT, so no edge was added despite the strong topical relationship.

The EITI report's citation of Décret 2007-184's Article 6 spending formula appears specifically in Section 5.2.17 (p.92), the mining-revenue transfers section, immediately following the Code Minier Article 95 discussion — not in Section 5.1.15 (p.57), the separate section covering the Code Pétrolier Article 146 petroleum-revenue split. No textual basis in the findings file ties the décret's 90/5/5 spending mechanism to petroleum-revenue transfers specifically, so no edge was added between the décret and the petroleum code, unlike the mining code (see dependencies above).

Checked villedeniamey.ne (homepage and /plan-strategique) for a Niamey city budget document; both pages contain only operational/performance indicators (roads, streetlights, sanitation) with no budget figures, revenue/expenditure data, or linked finance PDFs. villedeniamey.ne/actualites returned a 404. No named-commune budget document was found for Niger this round.

lesahel.org's article on the Cour des Comptes' 2021 Rapport Général (https://www.lesahel.org/gouvernance-au-niger-la-cour-des-comptes-rend-public-son-rapport-general-2021/) summarizes only aggregate figures (e.g., '46.27% compliance rate for state operations'); no individual communes are named, no link to the underlying report PDF was provided in the article, and no downloadable version could be located at courdescomptes.ne within remaining search budget.

Décret n°2014-137/PRN (Fonds de Péréquation / equalization fund), URL https://knowledge-uclga.org/IMG/pdf/decret_no2014-137_niger.pdf, was blocked on every attempt this round: robots.txt fetch failures (TLS hostname mismatch on the target's own certificate) and a proxy 403 on the Wayback Machine fallback. Content unverified; flagged in the findings file as a promising lead for a future pass since its companion décret (2014-136) was readable.

Décret n°2014-136/PRN (Fonds d'Appui à la Décentralisation), URL https://knowledge-uclga.org/IMG/pdf/decret_no2004-136_niger.pdf, was readable but contains no fixed percentage: Article 6 allocates funds by 'le deficit entre leurs charges obligatoires de fonctionnement et leur capacité de mobilisation de ressources budgétaires' (needs-based, not formulaic), and Article 7 defers exact modalities to a future joint ministerial arrêté. Not usable as a 'real formula/percentage' node this round.

Niger Ministry of Finance page 'Textes portant élaboration' (https://finances.gouv.ne/index.php/budget-1/reglementations-budgetaires/textes-portant-elaboration; note www.finances.gouv.ne fails TLS hostname verification, non-www worked) lists only state-level budget-process laws (Loi organique 2012-09, Décret 2017-429 on annual budget preparation); nothing commune-specific was found.
decentralisation-niger.net/index.php/regions/niamey contains only 2012 census population figures by arrondissement; no financial content was found.
